title: The naive framing: "does the app analyze the portfolio?"

title: A skill is a folder
text: It works. This one is client review. The skill MD file holds the full instruction set, plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it then acts. The file is the program.

title: Read, execute, return
text: The pipeline lives in the file step section. Claude reads the file, runs each step in order, and returns the result linear, no branching unless a step itself says so.

title: Spec it, or Claude reasons past it
text: Client review skill MD spells out exactly what to produce. A portfolio performance summary, allocation analysis, talking points, and action items ready before quarterly reviews, annual check-ups, or an ad-hoc client meeting. Feed it the same account data twice and it builds the same meeting-ready packet twice. Ask for something the file doesn't cover, a comparison it never mentions, a chart it doesn't list, and there's no instruction to fall back on. So, Claude reasons past the file on its own. title: Carry-out
text: Isn't a hidden analysis app. It's a plain text file of instructions. So, the same account data builds the same meeting-ready packet every time. Whatever that file doesn't say, Claude has to work out on its own. Your turn.

title: Your turn
text: Paste this into Claude. Write a skill MD for a recurring meeting you prep for. List exactly what must appear every time, then list what would be left to my judgment because the file doesn't cover it. Read back what Claude wrote. text: It. Same data, same packet, lay 'em in forbear.
